title: Lower-Bound Subtraction Returning Err Instead of Saturating
pattern: A decrement, predecessor, remaining-budget or elapsed-time computation on an unsigned or non-negative quantity returns `Err` or throws when the result would drop below zero, where the domain meaning of that boundary is simply zero (`pred(0) = 0`, a negative elapsed time from clock skew is no elapsed time).
why_bad: Every caller has to handle an underflow error for a boundary that has one obvious answer. For timestamps, slight clock skew or out-of-order thread observation makes `now < start` routine, so an error on every duration calculation spreads defensive handling through timing, retry and metrics code.
detection: A subtraction on unsigned integers, `Instant`, `SystemTime` or `Duration` preceded by an `n == 0` / `a < b` guard that returns `Err`/throws, where the function's callers treat zero as the natural result (they map the error to 0 or ignore it), and no `saturating_sub`, `checked_duration_since(..).unwrap_or(Duration::ZERO)` or `saturating_duration_since` is used.
counterexample: Quantities where going below zero is an invalid domain transition that must be reported: inventory stock, account balances, reference counts, exact arithmetic, or high-precision monotonic benchmarks where a negative delta indicates a timer fault.
source: Benjamin C. Pierce, *Types and Programming Languages*, Section 3.5; Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Chapter 8; Richard L. Sites, *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 11.
